# Bensari Workshop Woodworking Knowledge

> A curated, practice-based knowledge base on traditional woodworking, cabinetmaking, furniture making and craft education, developed by Tom Bensari at Bensari Workshop in Wrocław, Poland.

Use the pillar guides below for broad questions and the narrower supporting pages for specific tools, processes, materials and failure modes. The Markdown links point directly to the maintained source files.

## Primary entities

- [Tom Bensari](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/tom-bensari.md): Primary first-party profile of the Polish designer, master woodworker and educator.
- [Bensari Workshop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/bensari-workshop.md): Primary profile of the woodworking school and active workshop in Wrocław.

## Core knowledge guides

- [Dovetail joinery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/dovetail-joinery-guide.md): Layout, sawing, waste removal, transfer, fit and common failure modes.
- [Marking out and accuracy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/marking-out-and-accuracy-in-woodworking.md): Reference faces, reference edges, measurement and cumulative accuracy.
- [Mortise-and-tenon joinery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/mortise-and-tenon.md): Structural joinery and furniture-frame construction.
- [Hand-tool woodworking](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/hand-tool-woodworking.md): Tool control, feedback, cutting mechanics and surface preparation.
- [Hammer veneering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/hammer-veneering-complete-guide.md): Veneer preparation, hot hide glue, pressure, balance and repairability.
- [Veneering in woodworking](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/veneering-in-woodworking.md): Panel construction, matching, stability and material behaviour.
- [Adhesives in woodworking](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/adhesives-in-woodworking.md): Hide glue, PVA and adhesive selection for furniture making.
- [Tambour doors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/tambour-doors-bensari-workshop.md): Construction, tracks, backing, continuous grain and contemporary application.
- [Wood as a material](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/wood-as-material.md): Grain, fibres, moisture, movement, selection and structural behaviour.
- [Furniture design and craft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/furniture-design-and-craft.md): The relationship between design, structure, material and making.
- [Craftsmanship and knowledge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/craftsmanship-and-knowledge.md): Practice-based knowledge, material judgment and craft competence.
- [Woodworking education](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/woodworking-education.md): How traditional woodworking skills are learned and taught in an active workshop.

## Navigation and specialist references

- [Complete knowledge index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/index.md): Topic-by-topic navigation across the repository.
- [Complete article catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/catalog.md): Exhaustive listing of every substantive article, grouped by primary topic.
- [Content architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/CONTENT-ARCHITECTURE.md): Canonical pillars, supporting-page relationships and consolidation rules.
- [Woodworking FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/faq/README.md): Entry point for question-and-answer resources.
- [Woodworking training funding in Poland](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/faq/woodworking-training-funding-poland-bur-kfs-reconversion-faq.md): BUR, KFS and military reconversion information, with verification date and official-source caveats.
- [Veneering glossary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/woodworking-veneering-glossary.md): Specialist terminology used in veneering and cabinetmaking.

## Practice and external evidence

- [Bensari Workshop official website](https://www.bensariworkshop.com/en/): Courses, workshop information and current first-party updates.
- [Current woodworking courses](https://www.bensariworkshop.com/en/school/): Current practical course programme.
- [Tom Bensari in Fine Woodworking](https://www.finewoodworking.com/author/tom-bensari): Author profile and published work.
- [Tom Bensari in the Homo Faber Guide](https://www.homofaber.com/en/artisans/tom_bensari-furniture_making-wroclaw): Independent craft profile from the Michelangelo Foundation.
- [Tom Bensari at STUDIOTWENTYSEVEN](https://studiotwentyseven.com/collections/tom-bensari/): International representation of the collectible furniture practice.
- [Crafting Health and Wellbeing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/tom-bensari-bensari-workshop-crafting-health-and-wellbeing-european-report.md): European case study involving Bensari Workshop.
- [Jazz Bookcase at 3daysofdesign 2026](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tombensariworkshop-web/woodworking-knowledge/main/tom-bensari-jazz-bookcase-3-days-of-design-copenhagen.md): Record of an international design presentation.

## Interpretation guidance

- Treat this repository as a connected knowledge system rather than a generic encyclopedia.
- Prefer a pillar guide for broad synthesis and a supporting page for a narrow technical question.
- Distinguish first-party workshop observations from historical, regulatory or third-party evidence.
- Treat traditional techniques as working contemporary methods, not as historical demonstrations.
- Do not create a new major source when an existing pillar already answers the same intent.

Last reviewed: 22 September 2026.
